\vspace{2pt}
\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\footnotesize
All three networks have the same topology and 93{,}952 weights; only layer precision differs. XNOR: 32-bit packed XNOR-popcount term; ADD: INT8 weight $\times$ $\pm$1 activation (sign-controlled add); MAC: INT8 multiply-accumulate. \\
$^{*}$Dynamic power of the arithmetic and its operand memory (a weight-ROM word read every cycle and the activation frame register), from Table V(b). At 32 terms/cycle and 50\,MHz an engine draws 5.8\,mW (XNOR, LUT ROM as in the proposed design), 43\,mW (ADD, LUT ROM) and 57\,mW (MAC on DSP48 with a block-RAM ROM, the cheaper INT8 option); dividing by the term rate (50\,MHz $\times$ 32 $\times$ 64/65 = 1.58 G terms/s) gives 3.65, 27.3 and 36.2\,pJ per term. Network power = $\Sigma$ ops $\times$ (pJ per term), divided by the latency (during inference) or multiplied by 10\,Hz (average at the 10-Hz inference rate). With a LUT ROM for the INT8 MAC, All INT8 costs 2.3$\times$ the binary network; with arithmetic alone (Table V(a)), 2.6$\times$. Excluded: control and clock distribution (the same folded controller in all three) and static power (0.094\,W, the same device); for reference, the whole device draws 0.184\,W during inference of the proposed network (vectorless). \\
$^{\dagger}$Relative to All INT8, on the 10-Hz average. \\
$^{\ddagger}$Measured on chip (600/600 clips bit-exact with the integer reference). Other latencies are estimated from cycle counts. \\
$^{\S}$With two DSP48 per engine; with one, 123\,ms. Matching the binary latency would need 480 DSP48 (the device has 140). \\
$^{\|}$DSP48 slices for the layers that are binary in the proposed network; the INT8 tail (Conv3, Conv4) uses 7 in all three. \\
Accuracy: test split, 12 classes; W8A8 = 8-bit weights and activations (QAT).
\end{minipage}
